definitions.explanation: Deciding to deal with something later rather than now. Often implies deprioritizing something.

examples.japanese: {嫌|いや}な{仕事|しごと}を{後回|あとまわ}しにしてしまう。
examples.english: I tend to put off unpleasant work.

examples.japanese: {健康診断|けんこうしんだん}を{後回|あとまわ}しにしないでください。
examples.english: Please don't put off your health checkup.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}のことは{後回|あとまわ}しにして、{家族|かぞく}を{優先|ゆうせん}した。
examples.english: I put my own needs aside and prioritized my family.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{後|あと} (later) + {回|まわ}し (turning/sending, from {回|まわ}す)
Literally: "turning to later"

USAGE:
{後回|あとまわ}し is typically used with にする to form the expression "to put off" or "to postpone."

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{後回|あとまわ}しにする - to put off, to postpone
・{後回|あとまわ}しにされる - to be put on the back burner
・〜を{後回|あとまわ}しにして - putting ~ aside

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{先延|さきの}ばし - postponement, procrastination
・{延期|えんき} - postponement (more formal)
・{後|のち}にする - to do later

NOTE:
{後回|あとまわ}しにする often has a slight negative connotation, suggesting something is being avoided or deprioritized.

REGISTER:
Casual to neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
